answer: Run each epoch as a staked head-to-head tournament. Identities are paired at random, both answer the same task, say forecasting when a zephyr will calm the ocean swell off a pier, and a neutral jury awards the winner both entry stakes. Clones that draw each other just shuffle coins between their own pockets, while those facing strangers win only on quality. Splitting one operator into three hundred seats adds entry fees, not edge: if its model misjudges an opal's grade, it loses that bout three hundred times over.
